papers.title: Code for "Cross-Network NetFlow Intrusion Detection: A Controlled Benchmark of Transfer, Adaptation and Target Reference Windows" (Zenodo code+results deposit for an unpublished/under-review paper)
papers.opened: code (README, docs/EXPERIMENTS.md, crossnet/preprocess.py, experiments/feature_groups.py) read 2026-11-24 session 2; paper text still not public
papers.what_it_does: Code/run-level results: 18 detection and adaptation methods under leave-one-testbed-out evaluation on four NetFlow testbeds in both NF-v2 and NF-v3, equal source-only tuning, ten seeds, pre-declared hypotheses; 'target reference windows' suggests unlabeled/limited target data used for adaptation or thresholds.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Covered (from code): BRN = per-testbed benign-referenced z-scoring with a target benign window (== our PEN); DomNorm control; E7 drop-group XGBoost ablation (TTL, TCP window, timing, all artefacts incl. ports) on target AUROC and target-benign FPR; E2 failure decomposition benign vs seen vs novel attack families; E6 pairwise transfer with benign divergence audit (PSI, Wasserstein, SMD). NOT seen in code: counterfactual 'transplant' of single feature groups; LightGBM; random-vs-chrono pools; ESF-style data-driven environment-feature selection.
papers.datasets: NF-v2 and NF-v3: four NetFlow testbeds

papers.title: Is It Transfer? A Target-Only Control Finds No Consistent Source Benefit in Few-Shot Cross-Dataset Intrusion Detection on NetFlow
papers.what_it_does: On all four NetFlow v3 datasets, 12 directed pairs, RF/GBT/NN; compares pooled, importance-weighted, fine-tuned adaptation vs target-only training; domain classifier separability analysis; TTL-artifact removal check; shows per-domain feature scaling corrupts separability measurements.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Focus is few-shot transfer vs target-only (needs target labels); not leave-one-dataset-out with pooled sources and source-only thresholds; no benign-relative normalization remedy proposed.
papers.relevant_numbers: 540 comparisons: source significantly helps in 8%, hurts in 38% (uncorrected); mean F1 change -0.044 (95% CI -0.066 to -0.022); domain classifier AUC >= 0.996 for every pair on raw features; 23-40 of 45 features must be removed before AUC < 0.9; published zero-shot F1 of 0.81 does not reproduce on v3.
papers.fulltext_attempt: 2026-11-24 s2: preprints.org returns 403 to curl and headless Chromium; no arXiv copy; abstract only

papers.title: Code and results for "Shortcut Learning Undermines Cross-Domain Generalization in NetFlow-Based Intrusion Detection: Evidence from a 14-Day University Network Deployment" (Zenodo deposit)
papers.what_it_does: XGBoost/MLP trained on NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018-v2, tested on 16.79M flows of an operational university network (Suricata labels) and on NF-BoT-IoT-v2/NF-ToN-IoT-v2; zero-shot cross-domain under feature ablation, OT and CORAL UDA, few-shot fine-tuning.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: V2 not V3; single source rather than leave-one-out over four; no per-environment benign normalization described.
papers.datasets: NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018-v2, NF-BoT-IoT-v2, NF-ToN-IoT-v2, private university network
papers.relevant_numbers: 16.79 million target flows; 400-flow label audit.

papers.title: Auditing the NetFlow versions of IoT and enterprise intrusion detection benchmarks: data quality, shortcuts and cross-dataset evaluation (Zenodo deposit + GitHub README)
papers.what_it_does: Record-level audit of NF-v2 and NF-v3 of NF-ToN-IoT, NF-BoT-IoT, NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018: duplicates/label conflicts, shallow-tree shortcut probes per class vs benign, in-domain and cross-dataset runs, replication of Layeghy & Portmann 2023, SHAP; README lists checks incl. dns_ttl_anomaly, src_port_signal, temporal-split exploration.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Excludes NF-UNSW-NB15; no remedy (normalization) proposed as far as the description shows.

papers.title: Cross-Dataset Intrusion Detection under Benchmark Shift: Directed Transfer, Probability Calibration, and Alert Burden
papers.what_it_does: Crossed transfer among three NF datasets; removes endpoint-oriented fields; source Platt scaling; fixed source-negative 99.5th-percentile threshold measured on targets.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Three datasets only (no CIC-2018), version not stated; endpoint removal hurt rather than helped; no environment-normalization remedy.
papers.relevant_numbers: Within-domain AUROC 0.9773 vs 0.5445 cross-domain; removing endpoint fields: AUROC 0.5881 -> 0.4990; source threshold alerted on 36.2% of target flows.

papers.title: Leakage-Controlled Cross-Dataset Evaluation of Self-Supervised Graph-Based Network Intrusion Detection

papers.what_it_does_not_do: V2, two datasets emphasised; graph AE not GBDT; no systematic attribution across TTL/window/DNS/FTP features.
papers.relevant_numbers: Port-only probe ROC-AUC 0.998 in NF-BoT-IoT-v2 vs 0.615 on NF-UNSW-NB15-v2; raw transfer 0.332 -> CORAL 0.926.

claim_table.claim: C1: LODO on NetFlow V2/V3 shows large collapse
claim_table.exact_difference_one_sentence: NO CLEAR DIFFERENCE — claim already done: leave-one-testbed-out on the four NF-v3 (and NF-v2) testbeds with source-only tuning is in Gazi et al. (P01) and directed-pair collapse on all four NF-v3 sets is in Rayamajhi (P02); our RQ1 can only be a replication/baseline.

claim_table.claim: C2: environment-signature features (TTL, window, ports, DNS/FTP) explain collapse
claim_table.exact_difference_one_sentence: Partly done: port shortcuts (P06, P20, P22), a 'documented TTL artifact' and near-perfect domain separability needing 23-40 of 45 features removed (P02), and shortcut probes on NF-v3 (P04) exist; what we have not found is a per-feature attribution of the *benign-distribution* shift to the LODO performance loss across all four V3 sets with controlled feature-group ablations (but P01's paper text was not available, so this may also be covered).

claim_table.claim: C3: per-environment/benign-relative normalization or invariant feature removal improves cross-domain NIDS
claim_table.exact_difference_one_sentence: Feature removal mostly fails in prior work (endpoint removal hurt AUROC in P05; TTL removal did not change P02's conclusion; SHAP/port removal gave small gains in P20) and DANN/CORAL/MMD are established (P10, P06, P34, P03); per-environment benign-relative normalization as a source-only LODO remedy on NetFlow V3 was not found, but P02 warns that per-domain scaling corrupts separability measurements, so it is an open but risky angle.

claim_table.claim: C4: chronological vs random split inflation, esp. NetFlow V3
claim_table.exact_difference_one_sentence: Split inflation is well documented on CIC-IDS2017/2018 (P41, P42, P43, P44) and IoT data (P23); Luay et al. (P08/P09) released V3 with timestamps but only analysed temporal distributions, so a quantified random-vs-chronological gap on all four V3 sets appears not yet published as a headline result (P04 has temporal-split exploration scripts on three V3 sets).

claim_table.claim: C5: threshold transfer / calibration across networks
claim_table.exact_difference_one_sentence: Source-threshold transfer failure is already quantified on NF datasets (P05: 36.2% of target flows alerted; P06: label-free benign thresholds) and elsewhere (P47, P48, P28); only a systematic LODO threshold-transfer analysis across all four V3 sets tied to the environment-signature mechanism remains, and P01 ('target reference windows') may cover it.
